paragraphs: A young man from Calcutta once went to visit his in-laws in a remote village, far away from the Ganga.
At dinner time he noticed something odd: people were standing around holding drums, as if waiting for a signal. His mother-in-law insisted that he drink a little milk before sitting down to eat.

He guessed it was some local custom and decided it was best to go along. But the moment he took a sip, the drums burst into sound on all sides. His mother-in-law, crying with joy, put her hand on his head and blessed him.

Today, she told him, he had truly done a son's duty. He lived on the banks of the Ganga, so his stomach was full of Ganga water, and the milk he had just drunk contained the powdered bones of his late father-in-law. Thanks to him, the old man's bones had reached the Ganga after all, and his soul had gained all the merit of it.
learn: Swamiji told this with a smile at how far blind ritual can go. Customs should serve real meaning; when we follow them without thinking, they can become absurd.
